findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be `None`, raising `AttributeError`
findings.body: In `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, `enable_advanced` accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. For users who are not members of the organization (or certain staff/token-authenticated requests where `organization_context.member` is `None` and `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`), evaluating `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` on every GET request to the audit logs endpoint, even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested.

findings.title: `self.paginate` does not accept `enable_advanced_features` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` breaks on `datetime` fields
findings.body:
When `use_optimized` and `enable_advanced` are true, this endpoint calls `self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, order_by="-datetime", enable_advanced_features=True)`. This fails in two ways:
1. `Endpoint.paginate` does not accept `enable_advanced_features` (or forward arbitrary `**kwargs` to `paginator_cls` unless supported by `paginate`), which will raise `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`.
2. Even if instantiated, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` implements `get_item_key` as `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))` and `value_from_cursor` as `cursor.value` (like `Paginator`, not `DateTimePaginator`). Because `order_by="-datetime"` orders by a `datetime` field on `AuditLogEntry`, `math.floor(value)` will raise `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, and passing raw integer cursor values into `build_queryset` will compare a timestamp column against an integer.

findings.title: Allowing negative `start_offset` on Django `QuerySet` slices raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 182-184) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886), `start_offset` is allowed to be negative when `cursor.is_prev` is true or `enable_advanced_features` is enabled, and is then used to slice a Django `QuerySet` (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice bounds (`if (k.start is not None and k.start < 0) or (k.stop is not None and k.stop < 0): raise ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`). Any request supplying a cursor with a negative offset (for example `cursor=0:-10:1`) will crash with an unhandled `ValueError` resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error.
